searches.reason: Test whether SASRec’s sampled binary loss learns easy discrimination without reliable top-10 ranking. Electronics’ weak margin tail motivates this direction, while strong Movies_and_TV training margins do not establish validation performance. Seek affordable multi-negative objectives, false-negative controls, and sampling corrections; compare using the fixed macro validation HR@10.

searches.reason: Challenge the assumption that one final sequence representation captures current intent. Seek practical architectures that separate recent intent, persistent interests, and elapsed-time effects using observed histories and timestamps. Treat satisfied needs and replacement intent as hypotheses, not available labels.

searches.reason: Explore a structural shift from item-ID similarity toward specific item relationships grounded in permitted titles, descriptions, and training interactions. Seek lightweight text encoders trained from scratch and relation-aware graphs that can distinguish complementary from substitutable items without external pretrained weights or unavailable metadata.
